Epidemics responded to in 2014: measles (riposte campaigns 'contre les epidemies de rougeole survenues a Berberati, Nola, Carnot, Paoua et Bria'), pertussis (Grevai, Kaga Bandoro), wild poliovirus in CAR refugees at Lolo (Cameroon); cholera appears only under 'La preparation a la riposte contre le cholera' (kits pre-positioned at Bocaranga, Ngaoundaye, Ndim, Cantonnier and Obo; joint MSP-OMS-UNICEF risk-assessment and training missions in Nana-Mambere, Ouham-Pende, Haut-Mbomou and Bangui). EWARS (SAP) from Dec 2013 in Bangui, Bimbo, Begoua, Jan-Feb 2014 Bouar/Baoro, Feb 2014 Kaga Bandoro, Sep 2014 Bambari; 'les taux de completudes des rapports se sont stabilises entre 90 et 100% a partir de la semaine 26 jusqu'a semaine 51' (Bangui and periphery).

Source: Cluster Sante RCA / OMS Bulletin annuel des partenaires du cluster sante en Republique Centrafricaine 2015
Description: Health Cluster/WHO annual bulletin for 2015 (PDF bulletin_annuel_du_cluster_sante_2015.pdf, posted 18 Mar 2016). Section 'Prevention et lutte contre les epidemies' 2015: measles flare-ups isolated or with rubella (riposte campaigns in 9 sub-prefectures, 150,965 children) and two human monkeypox epidemics - Bria (Haute-Kotto) Feb 2015, 10 cases/1 death, and Bakouma/Bangassou (Mbomou) from 4 Dec 2015, 9 cases/2 deaths by 31 Dec, investigated by MoH/WHO/UNICEF/MSF-B/MdM/MINUSCA with Institut Pasteur de Bangui; cholera only as a contingency plan ('Plan de lutte contre les diarrhees aigues aqueuses y compris le cholera'). Indicators 2015: 'Promptitude des rapports du systeme d'alerte precoce' 92%; '% des structures sanitaires fonctionnelles dans les zones ciblees' 81.7%. EWARS continued in Bangui and Bimbo and was extended in 2015 to Bambari, Ngakobo, Kaga Bandoro and Yaloke.
